So I discussed this with somebody from Adobe last week on Slack, he said to me that the new requirement from the Adobe legal team (which came after a lot of internal discussions), should be:

```
Copyright [year file created] Adobe
All Rights Reserved.
```

I totally agree that it's silly to change these copyright headers yet again, it has been changing way too often in the last 8 years or so. And I would love if we could just put it in an external file and reference to that and never have to change it again in the future, but the Adobe legal team disagrees with this approach for some unknown reason.

I also argued on Slack that the check in coding standards is too lose, as it only checks for the first line and you can basically put whatever you like after the first line, they agreed and they will fix this in a new version of coding standards someday in the future so it's clearer what is required.

So for now, can you please update it to only those 2 lines and use git to figure out the year each file was created and use that year. Thanks :)
